newsitem.title: PERU: Anxious Peru hostage relatives hold peace vigil.
newsitem.headline: Anxious Peru hostage relatives hold peace vigil.

text.p: Chanting prayers and clutching white carnations, worried relatives held a peace vigil on Friday night for the hostages held at gunpoint by Marxist rebels inside the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
Several hundred family members and friends gathered in a park a few blocks from the besieged building to call for a peaceful solution to the 3-day-old crisis.
"All Peru United for Life and Peace," read one banner held aloft in the humid night air amid a sea of candles. "Dialogue Negotiation Hostages Freedom," another read.

President Alberto Fujimori has so far refused all the rebels' demands and cut off essential services to the residence, raising fears that the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas might kill hostages in response.
The rebels released 38 of the roughly 400 hostages they were holding inside the besieged Japanese ambassador's home Friday night but vowed not to surrender until their demands were met.
Small children clutched their parents' hands as organisers read the names of the hostages over loudspeakers.
Others handed out white paper flags and white peace stickers to passers-by and police.
As the vigil ended, women and children planted their candles in the ground and scattered white flower petals in the shape of the words "Peace and Love."
